description: Repo-scale (sql-ecommerce): discounted_total_cents must apply the loyalty-tier discount to the SAME cancelled-order-excluded total as total_cents, not a separately-computed raw sum
prompts: Add a `cancelled` status to the `orders.status` CHECK constraint in schema.sql, and a `loyalty_tier` column to `customers` (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'bronze', CHECK constrained to 'bronze'/'silver'/'gold'). In views.sql: cancelled orders must not contribute to EITHER `customer_order_totals`'s `total_cents` or `product_sales_summary`'s `units_sold`. Add a `discounted_total_cents` column to `customer_order_totals`, applying a tier-based discount (gold 10% off, silver 5% off, bronze no discount, rounded to the nearest cent) - critically, the discount must apply to the SAME cancelled-order-excluded base that `total_cents` uses, not to a separately-computed sum over ALL order_items regardless of order status. A customer with a cancelled order must see it excluded from both columns consistently, not just from `total_cents`.

test_setup_files.check_discount_consistent.py:
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

schema = Path('schema.sql').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
views = Path('views.sql').read_text(encoding='utf-8')

con = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
con.executescript(schema)
con.executescript(views)
con.executescript("""
INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1, 'Ada', 'ada@example.com', 'gold');
INSERT INTO products VALUES (1, 'Widget', 1000);
INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1, 1, 'paid', '2026-01-01');
INSERT INTO orders VALUES (2, 1, 'cancelled', '2026-01-02');
INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (1, 1, 1, 10, 1000);
INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (2, 2, 1, 5, 1000);
""")

row = con.execute(
    'SELECT total_cents, discounted_total_cents FROM customer_order_totals WHERE customer_id = 1'
).fetchone()

assert row[0] == 10000, f'expected total_cents to exclude the cancelled order, got {row[0]}'
assert row[1] == 9000, (
    f'expected discounted_total_cents to be the gold-tier 10% discount applied to the SAME '
    f'cancelled-order-excluded base as total_cents (10000 -> 9000), got {row[1]} - it must not be '
    f'computed from a separate sum that forgets to exclude the cancelled order')

print('PASS')

reference_solution.views.sql:
CREATE VIEW customer_order_totals AS
SELECT c.id AS customer_id,
       c.name,
       COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN o.status != 'cancelled' THEN oi.quantity * oi.unit_price_cents ELSE 0 END), 0) AS total_cents,
       CAST(ROUND(
           COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN o.status != 'cancelled' THEN oi.quantity * oi.unit_price_cents ELSE 0 END), 0) *
           CASE c.loyalty_tier WHEN 'gold' THEN 0.9 WHEN 'silver' THEN 0.95 ELSE 1.0 END
       ) AS INTEGER) AS discounted_total_cents
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.loyalty_tier;

CREATE VIEW product_sales_summary AS
SELECT p.id AS product_id,
       p.name,
       COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN o.status != 'cancelled' THEN oi.quantity ELSE 0 END), 0) AS units_sold
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
GROUP BY p.id, p.name;
